what_its_for: Elosulfase alfa is used to treat Morquio A syndrome (also called Mucopolysaccharidosis IVA or MPS IVA). This is a rare inherited disease where your body cannot break down certain sugars that build up in your cells. This medicine helps replace an enzyme your body is missing or not making enough of, which can help improve your ability to walk and breathe.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an IV (intravenous) infusion, meaning it goes directly into your vein through a needle or catheter. A healthcare professional will give you this infusion in a clinic or hospital setting. The infusion is given slowly over several hours. You should not try to give yourself this medicine at home unless your doctor and a healthcare team have specifically trained you to do so.
dosing: The usual dose is 2 mg per kilogram (2 mg/kg) of your body weight, given once every week. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose based on your weight. Each infusion typically takes about 4 hours or more. Your healthcare team will monitor you closely during and after the infusion for any reactions.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by a healthcare professional, it is important to keep all of your scheduled appointments. If you miss an infusion, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to double up on doses. Try to stay on your weekly schedule as best you can.
storage: Elosulfase alfa is stored and handled by your healthcare provider or pharmacy. The medicine must be kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). It should not be frozen or shaken. Once the medicine is prepared for infusion, it should be used within 24 hours if kept refrigerated. Do not use the medicine if it looks discolored, cloudy, or has particles floating in it.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting this treatment. Avoid getting this infusion if you are feeling very sick or have a severe infection, unless your doctor says it is safe. Do not skip your weekly infusion appointments, as consistent treatment is important for this medicine to work properly.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you have any signs of a serious allergic reaction or infusion reaction during or after your infusion, including: difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, chest tightness or pain, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, hives, rash, or severe itching, dizziness, fainting, or a sudden drop in blood pressure, fever, chills, or shaking, nausea or vomiting that is severe. Also call your doctor if you notice any new or worsening symptoms, or if you have concerns about how the treatment is working.
when_it_works: Elosulfase alfa does not cure Morquio A syndrome, but it can help manage symptoms over time. Some patients may notice improvements in how far they can walk and how well they can breathe after several months of regular treatment. Results vary from person to person. It is important to continue your weekly infusions even if you do not notice changes right away, as the medicine works gradually.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is approved for use in children 5 years of age and older. Younger children should talk to their doctor about whether this treatment is appropriate. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The effects of this medicine on unborn babies or nursing infants are not fully known. Your doctor will help you weigh the risks and benefits. Older adults: There is limited information on the use of this medicine in elderly patients. Your doctor will monitor you closely.
